title: Insert a New Range Into a Sorted List of Ranges

concept.title: Copy the ranges before the new one, merge all that touch it, then copy the rest
body: A list of ranges is **sorted** and no two ranges share a point. A new range arrives. Insert it, and **merge** it with every range it overlaps (two ranges overlap when they share at least one point), so that the list stays sorted and has no overlaps. For the list `1-3, 6-9` and the new range `2-5` the result is `1-5, 6-9`. For `1-2, 3-5, 6-7, 8-10, 12-16` and `4-8` the result is `1-2, 3-10, 12-16`.

Because the list is sorted, the ranges fall into **three groups** in this order. (1) Ranges that end **before** the new one starts (`r < lo`): they are copied unchanged. (2) Ranges that **overlap** the new one (`l <= hi`, and they are not in group 1): they are swallowed — the new range grows to `min` of all the left ends and `max` of all the right ends. (3) The remaining ranges start after the new one ends: copied unchanged.

body.code:
result = []
i = 0
while i < n and ranges[i][1] < lo:         # ends before the new range
    result.append(ranges[i]); i += 1
while i < n and ranges[i][0] <= hi:        # overlaps the new range
    lo = min(lo, ranges[i][0])
    hi = max(hi, ranges[i][1]); i += 1
result.append([lo, hi])
result.extend(ranges[i:])                  # starts after the new range

body: The program does one pass and no sorting, so it runs in O(n) time. The three-stage structure — "before", "overlapping", "after" — is the standard pattern for editing a sorted list of disjoint intervals. Ranges that merely touch without sharing a point, such as `1-2` and `3-4`, are **not** merged.

statement: A sorted list of `n` pairwise disjoint ranges `[l, r]` and one new range `[lo, hi]` are given. Insert the new range and merge it with all ranges that share at least one point with it. Print the number of ranges in the resulting list, and then the ranges in increasing order, one per line.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of ranges in the list.
Each of the next `n` lines has two numbers `l` and `r`: a range of the list. The list is sorted and the ranges share no point.
The last line has two numbers `lo` and `hi`: the new range.
outputFormat: The first line has `m`, the number of ranges after the insertion.
The next `m` lines have the ranges `l r` in increasing order.
constraints: For neighbours, r of the earlier range < l of the next one.

examples.note: The new range joins the first one: 2 ranges, 1-5 and 6-9.
The new range swallows 3-5, 6-7 and 8-10: 3 ranges, 1-2, 3-10 and 12-16.

hints: The ranges ending before lo are copied first.
The ranges starting not after hi (and not already copied) are merged into the new one.

explanation: The ranges that end before the new range are copied, the ranges that overlap it are merged into it, and the remaining ranges are copied after it.
solution.complexity: Time O(n), space O(n) for the output.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
ranges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]
lo, hi = map(int, input().split())

result = []
i = 0
while i < n and ranges[i][1] < lo:
    result.append(ranges[i])
    i += 1
while i < n and ranges[i][0] <= hi:
    lo = min(lo, ranges[i][0])
    hi = max(hi, ranges[i][1])
    i += 1
result.append([lo, hi])
result.extend(ranges[i:])
print(len(result))
print("\n".join(str(a) + " " + str(b) for a, b in result))
